children: The revised tariff structure raises ancillary costs as airlines increasingly rely on optional services to supplement passenger fare revenue

IndiGo has revised charges for several ancillary services, increasing the cost of add-ons including infant travel, excess baggage, unaccompanied minor assistance, priority services and travel certificates, according to media report. The changes will increase the overall cost for passengers who opt for these services during their journey.

The airline has increased the infant travel fee by 50 per cent to Rs 3,000 from Rs 2,000. The charge applies to infants below two years of age, who are required to have a ticket but do not receive a separate seat under the arrangement.

The revised fee means families travelling with an infant will now pay Rs 1,000 more than under the earlier structure. Based on an estimated 10 lakh infant passengers, a full Rs 1,000 increase across that entire base could translate into about Rs 100 crore in additional gross revenue.

However, the actual revenue impact would depend on the number of infant passengers subject to the revised charge. The estimate does not account for passengers who may not use the service or other exemptions and variations that could apply to individual bookings.

IndiGo has also raised its excess baggage charge to Rs 800 per kg from Rs 700 per kg. A passenger carrying 5 kg above the permitted allowance would now pay Rs 4,000, compared with Rs 3,500 under the previous fee structure.

The airline has simultaneously increased its unaccompanied minor fee to Rs 5,999 from Rs 5,000. The revision adds Rs 999 to the cost for passengers using the service, which is intended for children travelling without an accompanying adult.

Priority check-in and boarding charges have been increased to Rs 650 from Rs 450. The revised fee represents an increase of about 44 per cent, raising the additional amount payable by passengers choosing priority services.
IndiGo has also raised its travel certificate fee to Rs 300 from Rs 200. The charge applies separately from the base airfare and forms part of the range of optional services offered to passengers.

Ancillary services have become an important source of revenue for airlines, covering products and facilities such as excess baggage, seat selection, priority services and other optional offerings. These charges allow carriers to generate additional income beyond the headline ticket price.

For an airline with IndiGo’s passenger volumes, even relatively small changes in individual ancillary fees can have a cumulative effect on revenue and passenger spending. The overall impact will depend on the number of travellers purchasing each service and the frequency of such transactions.
